POLICY NOTE – 2016 - 2017

I. INTRODUCTION

“Crime is the outcome of a diseased mind and jail

must have an environment of hospital for treatment

and care”

- Mahatma Gandhi

The core objective of the Prison Department is to

confine the prisoners, deter them from committing

offences and to provide a conducive environment for

their physical and mental health, so that they can

reform themselves and be integrated with the main

stream of the society and be a fruitful citizen. With this

in view, regular academic opportunities are created

1

and a number of job oriented vocational courses are

conducted for the benefit of the prisoners. Further to

enable the prisoners to achieve right mental and

emotional balance, yoga and meditation classes are

conducted. Apart from this, to help the prisoners to

cope up with their individual needs, resolve family

responsibilities and to meet social obligations

counselling sessions are organized.

It is a universal view that sentence of

imprisonment is justifiable if it ultimately leads to the

protection of society against the crimes. The

incarceration of the prisoners thus motivates and

prepares them for a law abiding and self supporting life

after their release.

This Government is implementing numerous

innovative welfare schemes for the prisoners that help

them in becoming economically independent and lead

a life with dignity after their release.

2

under the Home Department of the Government. It is

headed by a senior I.P.S Officer in the rank of

incharge of the five Ranges in the State with

administration of Central Prisons, District Jails, Special

Schools under their respective jurisdiction. The Special

14.1 Cluster

A Cluster as defined by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, is a group of enterprises located within an identifiable and as far as practicable, contiguous area and producing same/similar products/services. The essential characteristics of enterprises in a cluster are (a) similarity or complementarity in the methods of production, quality control and testing, energy consumption, pollution control, etc (b) similar level of technology and marketing strategies / practices (c) channels for communication among the members of the cluster (d) common challenges and opportunities.

14.2 Consumer

Consumer means persons and families purchasing and receiving processed food products in order to meet their personal needs.

14.3 Food Processing

Food processing shall include process under which any raw product of agriculture, dairy, animal husbandry, meat, poultry or fishing is transformed through a process (involving employees power, machines or money) in sucha way that its original physical properties undergo a change and if transformed,

the product has commercial value and is suitable for human and animal consumption. It also includes process of value addition to produce products through methods such as preservation, addition of food additives, drying with a view to preserve food substances in an effective manner, enhance their shelf life and quality.

14.4 Food Business Operator / Entrepreneur

As defined in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, Food business operator in relation to food business means a person by whom the business is carried on or owned and is responsible for ensuring the compliance of the Act.

14.5 Food Safety

As defined in the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, Food Safety means assurance that food is acceptable for human consumption according to its intended use.

14.6 Food Parks

Food Parks will be a place where food processing units are established predominantly for production of processable agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, meat, poultry, dairy and fisheries products and notified under specific norms as may be prescribed.
